Declare the estimand of a pollination experiment

Source: R/estimand.R
pollin_estimand.Rd

Names the contrast, the scale it is reported on and the basis of any share, for a declared pollin_design(). Two estimand families are available:

Usage

pollin_estimand(design, family, scale, basis, population = "trial")

Arguments

design

A pollin_design() object.

family

"deficit" or "dependence". There is no default.

scale

One of "difference", "ratio", "rii" or "lnrr". There is no default.

basis

"loss" or "gain". There is no default.

population

The population the estimand refers to: "trial" (the default, the units in the experiment) or a pollin_population() object, strata of one column weighted by area. A population estimand is fitted with the strata as by and read with pollin_draws().

Value

An object of class pollin_estimand: a list holding design, family, scale, basis, population, the contrast (the treatment levels of the high and low arms) and the assumptions table.

Details

  • "deficit" (E1): supplemented versus open, the yield gap left by the pollination the crop received.

  • "dependence" (E2): excluded versus the design's reference arm (open, or supplemented), the yield owed to pollinators.

Writing high for the expected response in the higher arm (open or supplemented) and low for the lower one, the scales are:

ScaleValue
"difference"high - low
"ratio", basis = "loss"1 - low / high, the share of high lost without the contrast
"ratio", basis = "gain"high / low - 1, the gain over low
"rii"(high - low) / (high + low), equal to D / (2 - D) for the loss share D
"lnrr"log(high / low)

A loss share and a gain share answer different questions: an excluded arm yielding 75% of the open arm is a 25% loss share and a 33% gain. basis has no default; every analysis states it. It changes the value only on the ratio scale and is recorded on every scale.

See also

pollin_assumptions() for the assumptions the estimand rests on.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  pods = rpois(48, 30),
  trt = rep(c("Cage", "Open"), 24),
  Site = rep(letters[1:4], each = 12)
)
pd <- pollin_data(df, "pods", "trt", unit = "Site")
ds <- pollin_design(pd, c(excluded = "Cage", open = "Open"), "multi_site")
pollin_estimand(ds, family = "dependence", scale = "ratio", basis = "loss")
#> <pollin_estimand>
#>   family     : dependence (E2) 
#>   contrast   : Open vs Cage 
#>   scale      : ratio 
#>   basis      : loss 
#>   population : trial 
#>   layout     : multi_site 
#>   assumptions: 6 ; see `pollin_assumptions()`
